title: Daylight probe docket - personal experiment tracker
content:
Purpose: quick, day-to-day capture of small inference experiments I run on my dev cluster (1xA10). Keep things tiny and actionable — table + a short notes area.

TABLE (CSV-style):
date,exp_id,model,quant,batch,seq_len,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_sec,kv_cache_hits,notes
2024-09-18,dp-09a,redwood-7b,8bit,1,128,42,110,320,0,initial single-shot run, default runtime kernels
2024-09-20,dp-09b,redwood-7b,4bit,4,128,35,98,870,0,aggressive quant + batching -> throughput up, p95 dropped
2024-09-23,dp-10a,redwood-7b,4bit,4,512,120,360,780,0,seq len up; p95 ballooned, need prefix cache
2024-09-25,dp-10b,redwood-7b,4bit+kv,4,512,85,180,1200,1,enabled KV prefix caching, big p95 improvement; observed ~1.5x TPS
2024-09-29,dp-11a,redwood-7b-quant128,8bit,8,64,30,70,1400,0,try quant128 kernel, small seqs, nice latency and high TPS
2024-09-30,dp-11b,redwood-7b-quant128,8bit,8,64,29,68,1450,0,re-ran after warmup, stable

Quick takeaways (informal):
- KV cache gives disproportionate p95 wins for longer contexts; add to standard perf checklist for chat flows.
- 4-bit quant + batching helps tokens/sec but watch p95 at long seq_len. Always run seq=512 baseline before rolling.
- quant128 (mixed kernel) seems to hit a sweet spot for short-to-medium sequences when batch > 4.

To-dos / experiments to queue:
- [ ] dp-12: validate 4bit + kv cache under sustained 90% CPU/GPU util load (run 3h)
- [ ] dp-13: compare redwood-7b vs redwood-7b-v2 perf on A10 (same quant profile)
- [ ] dp-14: micro-A/B for routing policy: prefer 8bit cheap vs 4bit high-quality when latency < 100ms

Notes to self (scratch):
- Observed occasional 1-2% token corruption on 4bit on last run dp-09b; could be sampling randomness (check seed) or quant noise. Log outputs and re-run deterministic seed.
- Slack note: pinged @Maya for help on long-run harness (see linked_artifacts).
- Quick math: cost estimate rough: 1k tokens/sec @ 1450 tps ~ 0.69M tokens/hr -> if price is $0.01/1k tokens => ~$6.9/hr (local dev calc, not bill).

Short checklist before I copy into a PR/Confluence:
- Make dp-12 reproducible script in tools/bench (shell + docker)
- Add minimal repro artifacts: prompt, model-commit, runtime-args
- Capture raw logs (p50/p95) and attach to PR as CSV

Scratch questions (unresolved):
- Did dp-10b change kernel selection thresholds? check runtime logs for kernel name.
- How sensitive is perf to transient network noise on dev cluster (observed a 20ms spike on 2024-09-23 run)? worth adding network baseline checks.

Useful commands I ran (notes):
- ./bench/run_local.sh --model redwood-7b --quant 4bit --batch 4 --seq 512 --out /tmp/dp-10b.log
- jq '.metrics | {p50,p95,tps}' /tmp/dp-10b.log

End quick log. This doc is ephemeral and will be pruned once I move reproducible runs to tools/bench and a Confluence summary.
